Title: Contract one valuable security decision
Scope: Interview 6-8 relevant prospects. Select one repeated approval or remediation problem, one provider and the existing alternative. Produce a capability matrix: implemented, qualified, preview and unsupported. Agree deployment and data handling before promising dates.
Definition of Done: (1) A charter names budget owner, sponsor, platform/access owner and risk reviewer. (2) It fixes supported resources, 5-8 candidate controls, baseline effort, acceptance sample, data boundary, price and decision date. (3) A specimen evidence pack shows the additional decision/evidence AI Grid provides beyond existing tools. (4) A signed paid pilot/PO is recorded separately as the commercial gate; interview completion is not a sale.
Acceptance evidence: signed charter or documented rejection reasons, baseline worksheet and capability matrix.
Boundary: no commitment to enterprise-wide discovery or a bank-wide rollout.

Title: Qualify one secure customer environment
Owner and approver: E; C approves boundary; X assesses security
Dependencies: Y1-01; Y1-15 if private collection is mandatory
Scope: Reuse JWT, roles, tenant isolation and deployment configuration. Complete one customer IdP path, read-only permissions, secret handling, support access, deletion/retention and audit events. Choose one supported deployment model.
Definition of Done: (1) Customer approves data flow, region, retention, subprocessors and access scopes. (2) Production-profile authentication, forbidden-role, cross-tenant negative tests, session/revocation behavior and audited privileged access pass. (3) Raw prompts, responses, credentials and tool arguments are excluded from the initial collection boundary and tested with seeded sensitive data. (4) Demo data and auto-approval are off; synthetic approvals cannot satisfy release gates. (5) Before sensitive customer data enters the pilot, a basic backup/restore and incident-response path is exercised; independent review of that boundary is complete with critical/high findings remediated. Full production qualification follows Y1-08.
Acceptance evidence: configuration manifest, IdP/isolation/privacy results, assessment closure and customer approval.
Boundary: a sanitized evaluation does not qualify production operation.

Title: Make one provider's discovery dependable
Scope: Qualify the existing collector for the actual buyer's AWS, Azure or supported Copilot environment. Cover stable IDs, pagination, throttling, retries, permission failures, stale evidence and deletion semantics. Publish supported resource and relationship types.
Definition of Done: (1) Inventory finds at least 95% of independently enumerated supported in-scope resources; every discrepancy is explained. (2) Unsupported types and inaccessible scopes appear separately. (3) Fourteen consecutive days meet the agreed daily collection schedule; failures alert and cannot create a pass. (4) A usable baseline arrives within seven business days after access readiness. (5) Customer identifies owners for every designated critical AI system, or the ownership gap is explicitly open.
Acceptance evidence: reference export, reconciliation report, 14-day health record and permission/error tests.
Boundary: resource discovery is not proof of use; no all-cloud parity claim.

Title: Reconcile declared intent with observed assets
Dependencies: Y1-03 and a customer declaration sample
Scope: Add one CSV or narrow API import from the bank's registry/CMDB. Store customer IDs and field authority for owner, purpose, environment, provider, region, allowed legal entity/permitted data scope where applicable, classification, approver and approval expiry. Preserve a normalized AI Grid evidence inventory.
Definition of Done: (1) Seeded matched, observed-undeclared, declared-unobserved and conflicting/drifted cases produce correct, reviewable states. (2) Stable keys, duplicate handling and manual match decisions are auditable; ambiguous records are not silently merged. (3) Every imported/observed field retains source and timestamp. (4) Stale imports or collector failure cannot erase assets or imply decommissioning. (5) Customer reviewer accepts discrepancies and assigns resolution owners.
Acceptance evidence: versioned sample import, matching contract, seeded-case results and discrepancy sign-off.
Boundary: two-person implementation is import/export; bidirectional registry ownership and synchronization are deferred.

Title: Release a small, validated control pack
Owner and approver: E; independent policy reviewers and C approve
Scope: Select 5-8 evidence-supported controls spanning ownership/registration, approved location/provider, service identity, excessive tool/data reach, logging freshness or unsupported guardrail configuration. Identity and approved-scope checks belong to this pack, not another parallel product.
Definition of Done: (1) Every control has source fields, applicability, severity, rationale and positive, benign, absent, stale and permission-denied cases. (2) Pass/fail/unknown/not-assessed behave correctly; reachability and observed misuse remain distinct. (3) Production release passes current digest-bound validation, bias and approval gates, including the configured 95% Wilson lower-bound precision requirement at 95% confidence and two independent reviewers for high/critical policies. (4) Three customer-agreed scenarios and one fresh verified fix are demonstrated. (5) Unsupported runtime/token-verification claims are removed.
Acceptance evidence: versioned answer keys, holdout results, release digest, approvals and reviewed customer cases.
Boundary: pilot precision metrics do not replace stronger release gates.

Title: Connect a finding to accountable, verified resolution
Scope: Reuse canonical AI findings and the existing ServiceNow path if relevant; otherwise use export or one small destination adapter. Implement ownership, severity, due dates, expiring exceptions, reopening and fresh reassessment.
Definition of Done: (1) Create/retry/reconcile is idempotent; repeated scans do not duplicate work. (2) Each ticket links to the exact evidence and policy version. (3) Open, accepted-risk, expired-exception, verified-resolved and reopened cases pass. (4) Two customer-owned cases complete the intended lifecycle, using sanctioned exercises if needed. (5) Ticket closure, policy disabling and risk acceptance are never reported as a verified fix.
Acceptance evidence: linked lifecycle histories, retry/failure cases and fresh post-fix snapshots.
Boundary: one workflow destination; no new ticketing platform or uncontrolled auto-remediation.

Title: Produce evidence a reviewer can reuse
Owner and approver: E and F; C accepts evidence
Scope: Create a compact application/control evidence pack and machine-readable export, with customer IDs, scope, result, source, timestamp, control version, exceptions and disposition. Map only relevant framework/control references with versions.
Definition of Done: (1) Every released pilot control is traceable from conclusion to evidence. (2) Export totals reconcile to the UI; missing and unsupported evidence stays visible. (3) Retention, deletion and legal-hold cases follow the agreed policy. (4) Two comparable reviews show a target of at least 50% less active preparation effort than the recorded manual baseline, with required evidence complete. (5) Reviewer signs acceptance or records specific gaps; a missed value target triggers workflow revision, not a claim of success.
Acceptance evidence: accepted packs, baseline/time logs, completeness checks and export validation.
Boundary: framework mapping is not certification; preparation time is measured separately from overall approval lead time.

Title: Pass the production operating gate
Owner and approver: E; X tests security; C accepts operations
Scope: Establish monitored service health, backup/restore, upgrade/rollback, support ownership, incident response and capacity limits. Exercise tenant-aware restoration and prevent restored data from crossing retention or access boundaries.
Definition of Done: (1) Witnessed isolated restore meets agreed targets, initially proposed RPO 24 hours/RTO 8 hours. (2) Thirty days meet the proposed 99.5% availability SLO with transparent downtime accounting. (3) At twice the contracted pilot load, queues recover after transient failures and key UI reads meet the agreed target, initially p95 <=2 seconds. (4) Independent production-scope security findings have no unresolved critical/high issues. (5) Upgrade/rollback and an incident exercise succeed; support hours and escalation are accepted.
Acceptance evidence: restore and load reports, SLO history, test closure, incident record and operating pack.
Boundary: stricter customer requirements need funded scope; no implied 24/7 global coverage.

Title: Convert the pilot into paid production
Window: M4-6; two people M7-9, gated by procurement
Scope: Run a joint readout covering incremental value, accepted evidence, verified treatment, deployment/support scope and annual commercial terms. Document unresolved procurement prerequisites and owners.
Definition of Done: (1) Security sponsor and reviewer accept the contracted product outcome. (2) Production admission passes Y1-08 and the shared release gate. (3) A paid production agreement or PO is executed; an evaluation extension is labeled as such. (4) The next review, operational owner and renewal/expansion decision are scheduled. (5) If no purchase follows, record product, budget, timing or procurement reason and make an explicit continue/change/stop decision.
Acceptance evidence: signed acceptance, contract/PO, mutual action plan and dated readout.
Boundary: this is a target dependent on a buyer, not something engineering can guarantee by month 6.

Title: Detect drift from approved scope
Scope: Reassess changes to owner, approved provider/region, material tool permission and component/model version. Store supplier, version, digest when available, approval and expiry, clearly labeled observed, imported, attested or unknown.
Definition of Done: (1) Each agreed material-change case reopens the correct control/review task. (2) Expired or revoked approval is visible and cannot remain an unconditional pass. (3) Two application reviews reuse the same scope template. (4) The customer records final approval; green posture alone cannot approve a use case. (5) Model identity/version gaps remain visible rather than filled with inferred provenance.
Acceptance evidence: change-case results, approval histories and version/source records.
Boundary: basic component context is not a model scanner, behavioral safety assessment or full autonomy certification.

Title: Repeat onboarding for a second independent customer
Owner and approver: F and E; second C accepts
Scope: Sell the same security decision, preferably on the same provider. Reuse installation, permission, validation and evidence templates. Keep customer differences in configuration.
Definition of Done: (1) A second independent customer signs a paid pilot or production agreement. (2) Usable baseline arrives within seven business days after access readiness. (3) Core installation consumes <=5 engineering days, excluding customer waiting, without an application fork. (4) Bespoke work is <=20% of pilot delivery effort, or the overrun produces a repeatability fix before the next sale. (5) Acceptance reuses the same core control/evidence contracts.
Acceptance evidence: paid agreement, onboarding time log, change/configuration record and customer acceptance.
Boundary: another business unit in the first bank is expansion, not independent repeatability evidence.

Title: Prove reliability, support economics and next demand
Dependencies: operating customer data; Y1-11 where available
Scope: Publish a customer scorecard for source coverage/freshness, unknown evidence, reviewed precision, verified fixes, preparation effort, service health and direct costs. Select next-year scope based on renewal and paid demand.
Definition of Done: (1) The last 60 days meet agreed collection/support targets or have accepted corrective plans. (2) Direct hosting, integration, support and founder delivery labor are recorded per customer. (3) Renewal or continuation intent and budget process are documented; actual renewal is recorded separately when due. (4) The same added capability is requested by two buyers, with at least one funding a pilot, before expansion is approved. (5) The board/founders choose one next investment and explicitly defer the rest.
Acceptance evidence: scorecard, cost ledger, renewal notes and signed investment decision.
Boundary: customer counts and gross-margin goals are planning indicators, not fabricated traction.

Title: Integrate specialist model-security results
Window: M10-12 at four-person capacity; otherwise Year 2+
Dependencies: Y1-10, stable core and a funded model-security problem
Scope: Import an existing scanner/evaluation report first. If a scanner invocation is necessary, support one artifact store and one format in a bounded execution environment. Attach source, tool version, artifact digest, scan scope and expiry to the application/component.
Definition of Done: (1) Supported benign and unsafe fixtures produce the expected labeled results; report the sample and known blind spots. (2) Unsupported format, encrypted/missing artifact, timeout and malformed-model cases remain unknown or failed scans. (3) Resource limits and untrusted-artifact handling pass security review. (4) A changed digest invalidates the matching prior result. (5) Two customer release/review decisions use the result.
Acceptance evidence: result schema, fixture report, isolation tests and accepted review records.
Boundary: ModelScan addresses particular unsafe serialization/code patterns; a clean scan or valid signature does not establish behavioral safety, fairness or training-data integrity. Choose this OR Y1-14.

Title: Prove one typed runtime evidence contract
Window: M10-12 experiment at four-person capacity; otherwise Y2-01
Scope: Integrate one trusted customer agent/gateway producer for actor, agent/version, action/tool, decision, approval reference and outcome. Test privacy and correlation before developing behavioral detections or enforcement.
Definition of Done: (1) The contract defines authoritative versus informational fields and provenance. (2) A 14-day pilot includes >=100 real customer executions and >=50 real consequential actions, with >=95% useful decision/approval/outcome completeness over those actions. Synthetic tests are separate and cannot satisfy operational qualification. (3) Agent correlation is >=90%; version correlation is >=80% over at least 50 version-applicable records. (4) Replay, duplicates, clock skew, revocation and redaction tests pass. (5) A reviewer can reconstruct ten sampled actions, with gaps visible.
Acceptance evidence: schema, labeled source corpus, completeness/correlation report and reviewed timelines.
Boundary: this experiment does not pass the existing multi-provider Program 2 gate or authorize production runtime policies. Choose this OR Y1-13.

Title: Qualify private collection when the first buyer requires it
Window: decision M1; delivery re-estimated before contract
Owner and approver: F and E; customer platform/security approve
Dependencies: explicit deployment requirement and funded capacity
Scope: Package one customer-controlled collector with an approved metadata egress contract to the agreed control plane. Choose one customer environment and install method. Separate collection location from control-plane hosting and full air-gap operation.
Definition of Done: (1) Customer accepts what leaves the environment, destination, encryption, credentials and retention. (2) Installation, least-privilege permissions, upgrade/rollback, network outage and secret rotation pass. (3) Logs and egress tests show no unapproved content transfer. (4) A second clean installation follows the same package/runbook. (5) Funding, support ownership and displaced roadmap items are signed off before production commitment.
Acceptance evidence: approved architecture, deployment manifest, egress/privacy tests and two installation records.
Boundary: this does not provide a privately hosted UI/database/control plane or air gap. If those are purchase prerequisites, qualify a separate funded scope or choose a different first customer.

Title: Qualify attributable agent action evidence
Owner and approver: E; customer producer owner and policy reviewers approve
Effort estimate: 5-8 engineer-weeks, less only if Y1-14 is accepted
Dependencies: Y1-12 investment gate and trusted producer access
Scope: Productize one actor/agent/tool/action timeline with delegation references, decision, approval, outcome, event identity and provenance. Record whether each link is asserted, observed or independently validated. Retain metadata minimization.
Definition of Done: (1) The source passes a versioned qualification contract and Y1-14 quality floors. (2) Authenticated producer identity, signing/transport trust as applicable, replay rejection and schema/version handling are tested. (3) A sampled action chain is reconstructible without treating natural-language explanation as authorization proof. (4) Missing events and untrusted fields cannot yield a pass. (5) Production release follows either the unchanged existing multi-source program or a separately approved adapter program with explicit scope and independent review.
Acceptance evidence: producer certification, labeled event corpus, privacy tests and release-program decision.
Boundary: no universal action attribution; no raw chain-of-thought collection.

Title: Assess readiness for a specified autonomy level
Owner and approver: E and F; C defines/approves autonomy profile
Scope: Represent a customer-owned action profile: allowed tools/data, material-action approval, least privilege, transaction limits where applicable, human escalation, stop mechanism and evidence freshness. Support an assessment and approval workflow.
Definition of Done: (1) Each required condition maps to observed configuration, validated runtime evidence or an explicit manual attestation. (2) Missing evidence prevents an unconditional readiness conclusion. (3) The customer's sanctioned execution boundary produces valid allowed, denied, approval-required and emergency-stop evidence in controlled tests; AI Grid assesses that evidence. (4) Two application reviews produce named, expiring customer decisions. (5) A material scope/version change reopens the review.
Acceptance evidence: versioned profile, linked tests, approved reviews and stop-exercise record.
Boundary: readiness for one agreed scope is not general agent safety certification. AI Grid does not own the customer's risk appetite or automatically grant autonomy.

Title: Supply trustworthy risk attributes to one policy engine
Dependencies: Y2-01, 02 and a paid policy decision use case
Scope: Export narrowly defined, signed or equivalently authenticated attributes to one OPA, Cedar or existing customer policy service. Include asset identity, state, evidence/control version, issued-at and expiry. Begin in shadow mode.
Definition of Done: (1) Trust keys/identities, audience, replay protection, revocation and expiry are tested. (2) Consumer behavior for stale/missing/conflicting values is explicitly approved and tested; fallback is chosen per risk, not universally fail-open or fail-closed. (3) Shadow decisions match a reviewed answer key. (4) Policy owner accepts bounded production promotion and rollback after a failure exercise. (5) Each decision is traceable to the exported attribute and source evidence.
Acceptance evidence: contract, security tests, shadow comparison and signed consumer acceptance.
Boundary: a read-only producer still influences enforcement indirectly; AI Grid must qualify that influence. No general policy engine or inline gateway.

Title: Attach security evidence to an AI release decision
Dependencies: Y1-07, 10; Y1-13 if scanner evidence is required
Scope: Produce a machine-readable evidence manifest for one application's release/version with control outcomes, component references, exceptions and validity. Integrate one CI/release workflow only when paid demand requires it.
Definition of Done: (1) Evidence binds to a stable application/component version or digest; changed inputs invalidate relevant results. (2) For export-only scope, the customer reviewer/consumer correctly interprets allowed, disallowed and expired cases. For an authorized blocking integration, a benign release proceeds and a disallowed/expired test release is held. (3) Missing or stale evidence follows the customer's explicit decision policy. (4) Emergency exception, expiry and rollback are auditable. (5) Two real release reviews use the artifact; blocking remains separately authorized.
Acceptance evidence: manifests, version-change tests, release histories and owner acceptance.
Boundary: export completion is distinct from enforcement qualification. A signature proves origin/integrity, not model safety.

Title: Integrate one bounded partner response
Priority and commitment: P2 funded option; choose versus Y2-06
Scope: Use an existing gateway, identity or tool-control system for one response, such as temporarily disabling a specific tool permission or route. Start with recommendation and explicit operator approval.
Definition of Done: (1) Detection/evidence, target identity and proposed action are unambiguous. (2) Customer authorizes the action boundary and permissions. (3) Dry-run, approval, execution result, idempotence, timeout and rollback cases pass. (4) A sanctioned containment exercise verifies effect using fresh evidence from the enforcement system. (5) Source outage and incorrect targeting do not cause an unapproved broad action.
Acceptance evidence: action contract, authorization, exercise and rollback records.
Boundary: no unattended general remediation or all-provider kill switch. Irreversible credential revocation needs approved credential-reissuance recovery and is outside the reversible automation track. Advisory output remains advisory until independently qualified.

Title: Add one complementary discovery source
Priority and commitment: P2 paid-demand option; choose versus Y2-05
Scope: Select one second cloud, repository inventory, enterprise SaaS or existing SSE/CASB/identity usage feed. Choose the source that closes the most valuable demonstrated blind spot. Avoid building an endpoint/browser fleet.
Definition of Done: (1) Two buyers request the same source and one funds qualification. (2) The adapter documents resource/event semantics, permissions, freshness and blind spots. (3) Supported inventory reconciliation is >=95% against an independent reference; event feeds use an agreed labeled sampling method instead of an invented asset denominator. (4) Duplicate/conflicting identities remain reviewable. (5) A seeded unregistered case and a known approved case are correctly distinguished.
Acceptance evidence: demand records, connector contract, comparison corpus and customer acceptance.
Boundary: cloud resources, repository mentions and employee use are different evidence types, never interchangeable proof of deployed AI.

Title: Earn renewal and operationally support the new scope
Owner and approver: F and E; C accepts service scope
Effort estimate: 3-5 engineer-weeks of planned improvement, plus reserved operations
Dependencies: installed base and any accepted expansion
Scope: Version support contracts, review policy quality, monitor telemetry costs and publish customer scorecards. Prepare only the assurance/certification work actual buyers require, with an independent auditor where needed.
Definition of Done: (1) At least one renewal or paid expansion occurs when contract timing permits; earlier intent is labeled as intent. (2) Every supported source has an owner, failure alert, upgrade policy and cost limit. (3) Three consecutive monthly reviews meet agreed support/quality targets or pause expansion until corrected. (4) External audit readiness evidence is complete for the purchased scope; auditor issuance is tracked separately. (5) Direct contribution margin and capacity are acceptable under a founder-approved business case that includes support labor.
Acceptance evidence: renewal/expansion record, operating scorecards, cost model and scoped audit evidence.
Boundary: no automatic promise of SOC 2, ISO certification, 24/7 support, or 10-15 customers.

Title: Trace selected cross-agent and cross-system relationships
Scope: Link one customer workflow across selected agents, identities, tools and systems, including a supported A2A interaction only if used by the customer. Distinguish configured connectivity, observed invocation and verified delegation.
Definition of Done: (1) Every reported edge carries source, timestamp, relationship meaning and confidence. (2) Five agreed change/exposure scenarios identify the correct affected applications and unresolved gaps. (3) Unobserved delegation or unsupported protocols remain unknown. (4) A customer reviewer reconstructs the supported workflow from exportable evidence. (5) A sanctioned failure/cascade exercise shows the limits of available visibility.
Acceptance evidence: relationship schema, scenario corpus, reconstructed workflow and exercise report.
Boundary: no universal cross-agent trust graph or guaranteed cascade detection. Pin protocol versions; requalification follows material changes.

Title: Make component provenance and evaluation portable
Priority and commitment: P2; minimal export possible at two people
Scope: Export a supported CycloneDX ML-BOM or equivalent documented component manifest with model/provider/version, known dependencies, provenance references, evaluation scope and approval validity. Import one specialist result if Y1-13 was deferred and paid demand exists.
Definition of Done: (1) Export validates against the selected schema/version. (2) Known, attested and unknown provenance fields remain distinct. (3) Version/digest changes invalidate applicable results. (4) A customer tool consumes the export and a reviewer reproduces two release/evaluation decisions. (5) Supplier claims and scanner findings retain their original scope and source.
Acceptance evidence: schema validation, round-trip consumer test and reviewed decisions.
Boundary: a BOM records composition/provenance claims; it does not prove model trustworthiness. Full training lineage may remain unavailable.

Title: Maintain continuous, reviewer-accepted assurance
Scope: Refresh affected controls after relevant changes, maintain evidence validity and publish current assurance by application/control. Reuse event notifications where trustworthy and scheduled reconciliation where necessary.
Definition of Done: (1) A 90-day evaluation achieves >=95% fresh evidence across applicable contracted control instances; stale/unknown/unavailable instances count as misses. (2) Every agreed material-change test triggers the correct reassessment or review task within the contracted refresh interval. (3) Two successive periodic packs are accepted by customer reviewers. (4) Ten sampled applications, or the full smaller population, have traceable chains for contracted controls with gaps disclosed. (5) Risk acceptance remains separate from verified remediation.
Acceptance evidence: 90-day denominator-based report, change tests, accepted packs and portable histories.
Boundary: measure assurance coverage for the contracted scope, not total organizational safety or legal compliance.

Title: Evaluate one RAG or memory trust boundary
Owner and approver: E with specialist partner; C authorizes data/tests
Dependencies: funded repeated demand, approved content access and test environment
Scope: Select one retrieval/memory workflow and a precise failure, such as cross-user retrieval or unauthorized memory writes. Prefer customer/specialist evaluation results to building broad poisoning detection. Define expected permissions and observed behavior.
Definition of Done: (1) Data access, seeded tests and sensitive-content handling are approved. (2) A labeled benign/adversarial corpus measures the selected failure with reported sample size and limitations. (3) Source attribution, expected authorization and observed retrieval/write are linked. (4) The agreed fix is verified on fresh tests without suppressing benign use. (5) Independent review decides whether to productize, keep as a service, or stop.
Acceptance evidence: approved protocol, evaluation results, privacy review and go/no-go decision.
Boundary: metadata alone cannot prove content-level poisoning detection; no blanket RAG safety claim.

Title: Qualify one fully customer-controlled deployment
Window: M29-34; earlier only as separately funded prerequisite
Owner and approver: E plus funded operations owner/partner; C approves
Dependencies: contracted demand and full lifecycle support budget
Scope: Choose one private control-plane hosting pattern, with UI/API/database, secrets, observability, storage and upgrades. An air-gapped variant requires a distinct offline installation, update and licensing/support design; it is not assumed included.
Definition of Done: (1) Customer validates network/egress, residency, keys and administrative access. (2) Two clean installations, one upgrade/rollback and a witnessed restore pass. (3) Vulnerability patching, backups, telemetry access and support responsibilities are contractually assigned. (4) Evidence export and retention/deletion behave correctly. (5) Customer or funded partner covers the required operational hours and accepts the support model.
Acceptance evidence: deployment qualification, tested runbooks, network verification and signed responsibility matrix.
Boundary: private collector, private control plane and air gap remain separately named products/scopes.

Title: Permit a narrowly authorized reversible response
Dependencies: Y2-05, strong source quality and independent safety/security review
Scope: Promote one previously qualified response from operator approval to a preauthorized rule for a narrow target class and condition. Preserve manual override, dry run, rate limits, audit and rollback.
Definition of Done: (1) Customer signs the exact trigger/action/target boundary and expiry. (2) Evidence spoofing, stale state, incorrect identity, repeated events and outage tests cannot cause an out-of-scope action. (3) Effect and rollback are verified in a sanctioned exercise at contracted load. (4) A canary period meets agreed false-action and recovery criteria before broader use. (5) Revocation disables automation within a customer-agreed, measured maximum propagation time; cached-policy and disconnected-consumer behavior pass the agreed tests.
Acceptance evidence: authorization, independent review, canary record, action/rollback proof and revocation test.
Boundary: no autonomous general-purpose remediation or guarantee of a universal response time.

Title: Demonstrate a durable, repeatable business
Owner and approver: F with E for support economics
Effort estimate: 2-4 engineer-weeks of planned productization, plus commercial work
Scope: Improve renewals, repeat deployment, support and partner delivery. Validate another segment only after the core offer repeats. Price expanded evidence sources and operating obligations explicitly.
Definition of Done: (1) At least two renewal/paid-expansion decisions succeed across the installed base when due. (2) Three consecutive monthly reviews meet approved contribution-margin and support-capacity thresholds. (3) Repeat onboarding uses the supported package without customer code forks. (4) Any delivery partner completes an accepted deployment using documented boundaries and escalation. (5) The next strategic plan is grounded in retention, paid demand and operating evidence, not connector count.
Acceptance evidence: customer cohort/renewal records, cost/support ledger, deployment records and next investment decision.
Boundary: capacity-based planning targets are three retained paid production customers at two people or five at four; these are hypotheses to revisit quarterly, not forecasts or maximum market potential.
